description: Georgia's special civil statute of limitations gives victims of childhood sexual abuse five years from age 18 to file a lawsuit. O.C.G.A. Section 9-3-33.1.
shortAnswer: Most personal injury claims are subject to a two (2) year deadline. In the State of Georgia, however, victims of childhood sexual abuse are given five (5) years from the date they reach the age of majority (which is 18 in Georgia) to file a civil action (a lawsuit). Essentially, a victim has until their 23rd birthday.

faq.q: Which Georgia law sets the deadline for childhood sexual abuse lawsuits?
faq.a: Georgia's special statute of limitations for victims of childhood sexual abuse is found at O.C.G.A. Section 9-3-33.1. It defines "childhood sexual abuse" as "any act committed by the defendant against the plaintiff which act occurred when the plaintiff was under the age of 18 years" and then lists specific illegal acts.

faq.q: What acts of abuse are covered by Georgia's special statute of limitations?
faq.a: They include, but are not necessarily limited to: rape; sodomy and aggravated sodomy; statutory rape; child molestation and aggravated child molestation; enticing a child for indecent purposes; pandering; solicitation of sodomy; incest; and sexual battery and aggravated sexual battery.

faq.q: Does Georgia's statute cover oral sex abuse even though it isn't listed?
faq.a: Georgia law defines sodomy to include both anal and oral sex. I note this because I do not want anyone to think that they are without legal remedy simply because oral sex is not listed in the statute.
